subject: SalesPlatform RFI — data export & cross-border assurance
messages:
From: Paula Gomez <paula.gomez@salesplatform.com>
To: rishi.malhotra@redwood.com
Cc: legal-qa@salesplatform.com
Date: Thu, 14 Jun 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: RFI: cross-border exports, DPF evidence and subprocessors

Hi Rishi,

Thanks for taking a look at our security/compliance RFI. SalesPlatform is finalizing our procurement review and we need a concise package addressing cross-border data export protections for user-generated content that will be processed by your inference APIs. Specifically we need:

- Confirmation of your controller/processor roles for hosted API vs Dedicated vs Private deployments.
- If transfers from EU -> US occur for hosted API, do you rely on DPF (Data Protection Framework) or SCCs? Any attestation document you can provide.
- Subprocessor list and your notification/change SLA for new subprocessors.
- Cryptographic key model: are keys customer-managed in Private? For hosted, is there tenant separation (KMS/HSM)?
- Retention and audit log evidence (sample log schema) and access review cadence.
- Any available DPA annex redline or standard warranty language.

We'd appreciate a short response today with attachments we can include in the procurement package. If you have a compact evidence pack (summary + attachments) that would be ideal.

Thanks,
Paula Gomez
Senior Procurement Manager
SalesPlatform Inc.

[Attachment request: please attach evidence pack PDF, subprocessor CSV, and any KMS diagrams]

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
To: Paula Gomez <paula.gomez@salesplatform.com>
Cc: marissa.cole@redwood.com, karthik.iyer@redwood.com
Date: Thu, 14 Jun 2028 12:37:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: RFI: cross-border exports, DPF evidence and subprocessors

Hi Paula — thanks for the clear list. High level answers below and I attached a short evidence pack for procurement. Attached: redwood_dpf_evidence_v1.pdf (summary + docs), subprocessor_inventory_202806.csv, kms_keyflow_diagram.png.

Quick summary:
- Roles: Hosted API = Processor (we process customer data per contract). Dedicated = Processor with isolated capacity (contractual isolation + dedicated tenancy). Private (VPC/on-prem) = deployment model where the customer can be controller of the deployment; contract options available to reflect controller/processor mapping.
- Transfers & DPF: For hosted API we currently rely on the EU-US Data Protection Framework (DPF) plus SCC-derived contractual language for customers that request it. The attached PDF contains our DPF self-certification reference and guidance on where logs and controls map to the DPF principles.
- Subprocessors: inventory attached. We notify customers 30 days prior to adding a subprocessor by default; expedited notifications can be negotiated in a DPA annex for enterprise deals.
- Keys & crypto: Private deployments support customer-managed keys (KMS/HSM). For hosted API we provide per-tenant envelope keys with strict multi-tenant separation; Customer CMKs (bring-your-own-key) is available for Dedicated in certain plans — details in the diagram.
- Retention & logs: We retain request metadata and audit logs according to the retention schedule in the PDF (default 180 days for request traces; configurable for Dedicated/Private). Audit log schema excerpt included.
- DPA annex & redline: we typically provide a standard DPA and can accept limited redlines; Marissa (privacy) and Karthik (security) are cc'd to confirm the technical specifics and follow up on any redline language.

If you want, we can schedule a 30-minute call Friday to walk through the evidence and any procurement language the legal team wants to propose.

Best,
Rishi Malhotra
Head of Sales — Enterprise
Redwood Inference

Attachments:
- redwood_dpf_evidence_v1.pdf (summary, DPF mapping table, SOC2 reference)
- subprocessor_inventory_202806.csv (vendor, region, service-type, contract-date)
- kms_keyflow_diagram.png (high-level key flow for hosted/dedicated/private)

From: Tom Henderson <tom.henderson@procure.salesplatform.com>
To: rishi.malhotra@redwood.com
Cc: Paula Gomez <paula.gomez@salesplatform.com>, legal-qa@salesplatform.com
Date: Fri, 15 Jun 2028 08:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: RFI: cross-border exports, DPF evidence and subprocessors

Rishi — thanks for the fast follow-up and attachments. A couple of clarifications the procurement/legal team asked for after reviewing the pack:

1) Subprocessor change SLA: your note says "notify customers 30 days prior" — can you confirm whether there is an option for a 45-day notice and an opportunity for customers to object before onboarding? We need this for our higher-risk categories.

2) KMS specifics: the diagram is helpful. For hosted API can you confirm whether the envelope keys are generated per-customer or per-tenant pool? Is the master wrapping key stored in HSMs with FIPS certification or a cloud KMS? We need to know the control point for key custody for EU-origin data.

3) DPF attestation: our legal team expects a short attestation statement or letter that we can include in our procurement file confirming Redwood's reliance on DPF for EU-US transfers and the date of the last self-assessment. If you have a template attestation we can include, please attach.

Finally, legal would like to propose a small DPA annex edit (related to subprocessor audit rights). Who should I send the redline to?

Thanks — can you have Marissa or Karthik respond to the technical bits and confirm timelines?

—Tom
Tom Henderson
Procurement Lead, SalesPlatform Inc.

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Tom Henderson <tom.henderson@procure.salesplatform.com>, Paula Gomez <paula.gomez@salesplatform.com>
Cc: rishi.malhotra@redwood.com, karthik.iyer@redwood.com
Date: Fri, 15 Jun 2028 11:20:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: RFI: cross-border exports, DPF evidence and subprocessors

Tom/Paula — Marissa from Privacy here; looping in Karthik (Security) for the KMS specifics. Responses below with concrete options we can include in the DPA annex or SOW depending on procurement appetite.

1) Subprocessor change SLA
- Standard: 30-day prior notice.
- Enterprise option: 45-day notice + limited objection right for defined high-risk categories (we can add machine-learning model tuning vendors and long-term storage as examples). If you require contractual objection + suspension right we can discuss a narrow carve-out — this is typically accepted for large enterprise customers with committed Dedicated or Private deployments.

2) KMS and key custody (Karthik note below is inline)
- Hosted API:
  - Envelope keys: generated per-customer logical key (customer-id scoped). Per-customer data keys are used for request-level encryption; they are wrapped by a cluster master key.
  - Master wrapping keys: stored in cloud HSM-backed KMS with FIPS 140-2 level 3 compliance in our primary US region. Access to HSM is restricted to a small number of operators under RBAC and logged.
  - For EU-origin data: we offer regional key residency for Dedicated and Private; hosted API customers can request EU-region wrapping keys on a contractual basis.
- Dedicated: customer can opt for bring-your-own-key (BYOK) with a KMS binding in the contract — keys remain under customer-controlled KMS where supported.
- Private (VPC/on-prem): full customer key ownership; Redwood can provide integration guidance for linking to on-prem HSMs.

Karthik (security) adds: "We perform quarterly key rotation for master wrapping keys and daily rotation for ephemeral request keys where applicable. All key access is audited; audit logs are tamper-evident and stored in the same retention window referenced in the evidence pack. We can provide HSM certificate snapshots (redacted serials) as evidence under NDA if required."

3) DPF attestation & self-assessment
- We can provide a short attestation letter confirming reliance on DPF for EU->US transfers and include the date of our last self-assessment (included in redwood_dpf_evidence_v1.pdf). We'll produce a PDF attestation you can include in the procurement file.

4) DPA annex redline
- Please send redlines to legal-qa@salesplatform.com (cc marissa.cole@redwood.com and rishi.malhotra@redwood.com) and we will review within 5 business days for standard enterprise terms; if the redline requests an expanded audit right we will propose language that balances audit access with our supplier confidentiality obligations.

Next steps: I can have the attestation + an updated subprocessor notice option (45-day + limited objection) sent by end of day Monday. If it's helpful let's schedule a short technical call — I'm available Monday afternoon PT.

Regards,
Marissa Cole
Privacy Lead
Redwood Inference
